Run 'claude update', or update the Claude desktop app, then try again.","details":{"error_code":"claude_code_version_too_old"}},"request_id":"req_011CegQu2xW5e5oLygDDqtHQ"}` (verbatim errorMessage from ~/.kpi/agent/sessions/--Users-leebarry-K-pi--/2026-09-03T11-17-14-058Z_*.jsonl) because packages/ai still identifies as claude-cli/2.1.75, and K-π surfaces it only as the raw assistant error. A2: the official Anthropic grant lives in two files with two refreshers — the base runtime refreshes ~/.kpi/agent/auth.json on every request, K-π refreshes its accounts.secrets.json copy (anthropic/default) at every session_start/turn_start; Anthropic rotates refresh tokens, so the copy that refreshes second is dead forever (invalid_grant), the slot is cooled 5h instead of told to re-login, and the warning embeds a full JS stack every session start and every turn.
design.root_cause: A1: packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts:77 pins `const claudeCodeVersion = "2.1.75"`, sent at :938 as `user-agent: claude-cli/<v>` (with `anthropic-beta: claude-code-20250219,oauth-2025-04-20` at :937) for every sk-ant-oat token (isOAuthToken :874-876). The server floor is now 2.1.251; upstream fixed it in 96317e50b (one line, 2.1.75 → 2.1.251, nothing else). In K-π the 400 reaches after_provider_response (index.ts:850) with no body, then message_end (:890) where classifyProviderBodyFailure (:930; QUOTA_TOKENS errors.ts:2) does not match the text, so the handler returns at :934 and says nothing. A2: one grant, two owners. (1) packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:583 prepareRequest calls getAuth(model) on EVERY request before transformHeaders (:593) runs K-π's before_provider_headers hook; packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:139-155 refreshes an auth.json OAuth credential with <5 min left under the auth.json lock and persists the rotated tokens. (2) store.ts:393-431 importOfficialCredentials copies auth.json's grant into accounts.secrets.json as slot `default` once (only when no `default`, :412); index.ts:559-585 refreshExpiringCredentials then calls oauth.refresh on that copy with the same refresh token. After either side rotates, the other side's refresh token is revoked (on this machine auth.json anthropic expires=1788453002792, the slot copy expires=1788387252486 — the base rotated, K-π's copy is dead). (3) index.ts:579 cools the slot DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS and :581 notifies error.message, which packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/anthropic.ts:330 builds from formatErrorDetails (:82-95, `stack=` at :92). (4) Every pooled OAuth login also lands in auth.json: index.ts:217 → model-runtime.ts:673-677 → packages/ai/src/models.ts:581 credentials.modify — so `/accounts login anthropic work` silently makes auth.json mirror `work` (two owners again). (5) When the base's own refresh dies, prepareRequest throws ModelsError("OAuth refresh failed for anthropic: …") whose message embeds the cause text via withCauseDetail (resolve.ts:30, :37-42), and packages/agent/src/agent.ts:511-524 turns it into an assistant error with that errorMessage; K-π's message_end has no pending response to pair (:898-899) and returns silently, so the operator is never told the grant in auth.json needs a new login.

errors.ts exports: `parseClientVersionRejection(text: string | undefined): { sent?: string; required?: string } | undefined`; `type RefreshFailure = { kind: "invalid_grant" } | { kind: "http"; status: number; summary: string } | { kind: "transport"; summary: string }`; `summarizeRefreshFailure(error: unknown): RefreshFailure` (summary never contains `stack=` or a frame, <= 160 chars).

before_provider_headers contract: for a slot with `official: true` K-π leaves the runtime's auth header untouched (it is that slot's grant) and only records request attribution; non-official slots keep having their header set from accounts.secrets.json.

Exact notifications, each at most once per session per key: `K-π accounts: ${pool}/${slot} needs a new login: ${reason}. Run /accounts login ${pool} ${slot}` (error); `K-π ${VERSION} identifies to Anthropic as Claude Code ${sent}; Anthropic requires ${required} or newer for ${model}. Update K-π: npm install -g @korallis/k-pi@latest` (error, key `${sent}->${required}`); `K-π accounts: ${list} now reads its credential from auth.json` (info); `K-π accounts: could not refresh ${pool}/${slot}: ${summary}; cooling ${n}m` (warning); `K-π accounts: could not reconcile auth.json with accounts.json: ${message}` (error); `Added account ${pool}/${slot} (${pool}/${previous} keeps its previous grant)` (info) when a login demotes the previous official slot.
Widget: a slot with needsLogin renders `<label> <pct>%… needs login`.

Normative sync rule (docs/spec.md §13, pending NH-03): per pool at most one official slot; auth.json[pool] ≡ that slot's grant; it has no secrets entry; K-π never calls oauth.refresh on it; non-official slots exist only in accounts.secrets.json and are refreshed by K-π; a pooled OAuth login the runtime persisted into auth.json becomes the official slot and the previous official slot keeps the grant auth.json held until then as a K-π-refreshed secret; reconciliation runs once per session_start, by content match, then the `default`/expired-copy legacy rule, else a fresh official slot.

risks: Legacy stores carry no `official` flag; reconcile binds by content match, then binds `default` only when its secret is absent or an expired OAuth copy, else creates a fresh official slot (slot-2). A legacy `default` holding an alive access token from the same account but a rotated-away refresh token is therefore not bound; it later dies with invalid_grant and is named once as needing login (`/accounts login anthropic default`), and the operator may then `/accounts logout anthropic default`. Visible and bounded, never silent.

A legacy split where K-π's copy is the live lineage and auth.json's refresh token is the dead one is not repaired by publishing K-π's copy (K-π never writes auth.json): the base's refresh fails at prepareRequest, the official slot is marked needs-login once, and the pool is unavailable until `/accounts login anthropic <official>` — one command, then resend the prompt (no automatic retry; agent-session.ts:2880 retries only kpi_account_failover). Automatic promotion of a live sibling into auth.json was cut as an unrequested account substitution.

Transient refresh failures (network, 5xx, timeout) keep the existing 5-hour cooldown bound on non-official slots; only the wording changed. A successful refresh on a later turn_start does not clear that cooldown (existing behaviour, unchanged).

Base `/logout anthropic` mid-session removes auth.json's entry while the official slot stays selectable until the next session_start marks it orphaned; in between, prepareRequest fails with `Provider is not configured` (or the runtime's env fallback serves an env token). Existing exposure, now reported at the next session start.

`/accounts logout` of the official slot removes the slot but leaves auth.json's grant; the next session_start re-imports it as an official slot (`default` or next id) — existing re-import behaviour, unchanged.
reconcileOfficialCredentials runs inside session_start under try/catch; a malformed accounts.json still fails loudly there (assertAccounts), as today, and startup continues without a pool.

design.issue: ISSUE B — the operator board is static and mute during a node run: stage cells show only id/label/DONE|CURRENT|PENDING, nothing on the board or in the chat changes for the minutes a node runs, no per-node elapsed/cost/tool activity is shown or even recorded, and the /kpi status overlay closes on any key instead of letting the operator select a stage and inspect what it did.
design.root_cause: Three gaps compound. (1) No refresh trigger while a node runs: installWidget (control-plane.ts:325-336) builds one BoardModel and wraps it in a component; the only rebuild path is dependencies.onStateChange (control-plane.ts:483-485), which gated-loop awaits after writeState at the end of a superstep (gated-loop.ts:1518-1519, after engine.runSuperstep() at :1396 returns), at runLoop's initial write (:1910) and after resumeLoop's terminal write (:1776). board-component.ts:38 refresh(model) exists but nothing calls it, so the board is frozen for the whole duration of an agent node. (2) No per-node data exists to draw: the engine sets nodeState.status = "running" only in memory (engine.ts:1324-1334) and checkpoints at the end of the superstep (:1412-1414) or on retry backoff (:1149); GraphNodeRunState (schema.ts:161-181) has no startedAt/elapsed/cost/model; recordSessionCost (engine.ts:816-825) computes a per-node cost delta and folds it into sessionCostUsd, discarding the per-node figure, and it runs once per attempt from executeNode's finally (:1000) inside the executeWithRetries loop (:1132-1134); the only per-node signal on disk is tool.request (policy.ts:963-971, node stamped from job.state.node) and nobody counts it. EVENT_TYPES/EventInput (append-log.ts:9-33, :83-151) and event.schema.json (:15 oneOf) have no node lifecycle type — the real run .kpi/runs/20260903-fix-claude-model-requests-failin-42986cfa/events.jsonl has 261 tool.request records and zero node.* records. (3) The board model has no activity slot and the overlay has no input model: stageCells (board.ts:239-251) emits three fixed lines, telemetryRegion (:464-476) has no activity row, and showStatus's overlay implements handleInput() { done() } (control-plane.ts:366-368). A verified constraint shapes the fix: while `/kpi <goal>` runs, the interactive main loop is blocked in `await this.session.prompt(userInput)` (interactive-mode.ts:1188-1191, the handler is awaited at agent-session.ts:1360) and further input is queued in pendingUserInputs (interactive-mode.ts:3176-3179) because the main session is neither streaming nor compacting (graph nodes run on sdk sessions, engine.ts:567) — so `/kpi status` cannot open mid-run and the always-on widget, ticking on its own setInterval, is the only live surface; the interactive overlay serves live-but-paused jobs (NEEDS_HUMAN/interrupted), which is exactly when an operator inspects what a stage did before approving.

risks: The widget tick does file I/O every second (state.json read, six stats, one events.jsonl stat and an incremental read of appended bytes only); the first read of a long log (tens of thousands of tool.request lines) folds it once, linear in size, and every later tick is O(appended bytes). Overlapping reads are coalesced into one in-flight promise, so an onStateChange reinstall or a slow disk never double-parses.

tool.request attribution uses record.node, which policy stamps from state.json.node (written at superstep end); both shipped graphs run one agent node per superstep, but a graph with two concurrent agent nodes would count both nodes' tool calls under one node. node.started/finished remain the authoritative per-node timing/cost regardless.

Verified: `/kpi status` cannot be opened while `/kpi <goal>` runs — the interactive main loop awaits the handler (interactive-mode.ts:1188-1191) and queues further input (:3176-3179). The always-on widget (its own setInterval) is therefore the only live surface during a node; the queued `/kpi status` fires after the job returns and, for a finished job, reports 'no active job — last job … DONE'. Opening the overlay mid-run would need a registered shortcut (types.ts:1350 registerShortcut) — see open_questions.

An events.jsonl append failure inside runSuperstep propagates and fails the batch, the same way review.verdict (engine.ts:1113) and emitTerminal do; a run store that cannot be appended to is treated as a broken run, not silently skipped (tool.request's swallow at policy.ts:974 is the deliberate exception for the tool hook, which has no batch to fail).

Adding two records per node attempt to events.jsonl changes record counts; audited tests filter by type (loop.terminal) and none pin totals, but `/kpi verify` output ('N records chained') and any downstream line-counting tooling will see more records.

problems.claim: The shared incremental ActivityReader is unserialized and its `newRecords` ("records appended since the previous read") is single-consumer, but the design gives it three concurrent callers: the widget ticker (guarded only by its own `busy` flag), `onNodeEvent -> installWidget -> buildBoardModel`, and the overlay's `load()`/`readNodeDetail` — all resolving the same reader from the module-level `activityReaders` Map keyed by eventsPath. Two overlapping `read()` calls both see the same `offset`, both parse the same byte range and both push into `records[]`, so toolCalls/toolsByName double-count and `accounts.failover` is narrated twice (contradicting the spec'd test 'a second tick does not repeat it'); conversely a non-narrating read (overlay or onNodeEvent path) that lands between two ticks consumes `newRecords`, so the failover line is silently dropped. The installWidget pseudo-code also references `snapshot.newRecords` although `buildBoardModel` returns only a BoardModel — there is no defined way for the tick to obtain the snapshot.
problems.evidence: Design change (c) for control-plane.ts: `activityReaders = new Map<string, ActivityReader>()` shared by buildBoardModel; tick callback reads `snapshot.newRecords` while calling `buildBoardModel(...)`. Design change (e): `onNodeEvent: async (event) => { ...; await installWidget(ctx, dependencies); }` runs while the ticker is live. board-activity.ts spec: reader 'keeps { path, offset, partial, records[] }' with no lock; compare append-log.ts:395-413 `withAppendLock` which exists precisely because check-then-act on a shared file cursor races. design.issue: ISSUE C: the gated graph has no operator gate after planning. `plan` returns stack.json and `implement` starts with no notification, no approval, and no way to request changes; the only human node is the release gate. The engine models a human answer as a bare boolean with a static question, so a plan gate cannot show the frozen plan or carry feedback back to the planner. In any non-TUI mode (print / no dialog UI) a human gate is answered by the harness stub (confirm → false) instead of stopping NEEDS_HUMAN with a resume command.
design.root_cause: Three gaps, one per layer. (1) Topology: packages/coding-agent/src/kpi/graphs/coding-loop.gated.json edge L192-195 is `plan → implement` unconditional; the single human node (L139-144) sits after review. (2) Engine: `HumanGraphNode` (graph/schema.ts L49-55) is `{title, question, statePath}` only; `submitHuman(approved: boolean)` (graph/engine.ts L1459-1492) writes one boolean at statePath and nothing else; `nodePrompt` (L697-713) substitutes only `{{job_id}}`, so a re-run planner (isolated session, no memory) can never see operator feedback. (3) Driver: gated-loop.ts answers every pending human with `ctx.ui.confirm(pending.title, pending.question)` in two duplicated loops (L1690-1726 resume path, L1932-1975 first run) and never checks `ctx.hasUI`; the no-UI stub (core/extensions/runner.ts L236-239) returns `confirm → false`, `select → undefined`, so a gate in print mode is silently denied and routed by `policy.onHumanDeny` rather than stopping for the operator. No bell/attention API exists in packages/tui/src (every `\x07` hit is OSC parsing), so "notify" today is only the board turning protocol-blue via `pending_question` (gated-loop.ts L464 → control-plane.ts L232 → board.ts L407-418).

risks: Behaviour change for the existing release gate in non-TUI modes: today the stub confirm returns false and the run is routed by policy.onHumanDeny (revise → another implement round); after this change it stops NEEDS_HUMAN with recovery `approval`. This is the defect the issue names (a harness-answered gate), so it is intended, but it is visible to anyone driving gated jobs through print/RPC without a dialog handler.

A gated job started without a dialog UI still spends research/specify/plan cost before stalling at the gate (see open question 2); the stall is recoverable with the exact resume command and no work is lost.

Every gated job now emits one more approval.result and, for a no-UI stop, one loop.terminal NEEDS_HUMAN followed by a second terminal on resume — the same shape the provider NEEDS_HUMAN path already produces. README record counts (14 → 15) change in three places (L582, L669, L887). `graph_round` (max node runs) rises by one per plan revision; per-node caps are independent, so implement's own run budget is not reduced.

The revision bound reuses the plan node's run cap (default 3 runs). An operator who passes `--max-rounds 1` gets zero change requests: the first Request changes ends EXHAUSTED. The dialog states `Revision N of cap` so this is visible, but it couples plan revisions to the same flag as verifier rounds (open question 1).

stack.json is rewritten on re-plan; an operator reading `.kpi/runs/<job>/stack.json` between gates sees the latest version only. The event log keeps the feedback and both approval decisions, so the history is reconstructible.

The select title carries a multi-line summary (bounded by PLAN_SUMMARY_MAX_MODULES = 12); the interactive selector already accepts multi-line titles (confirm passes `${title}\n${message}`), and RPC clients receive the same title string in extension_ui_request. There is no separate full-plan view: the dialog names the file path.

Feedback text is stored verbatim in the checkpoint and events.jsonl (redacted by redactJson for secret-shaped values), capped at MAX_HUMAN_FEEDBACK_CHARS = 4000. It is the operator's own words but it is durable run data.

design.issue: ISSUE D — the operator cannot see how K-π is concurrent. Graph nodes run as in-process AgentSession objects and only workerRole nodes (reviewer) become separate `kpi --mode rpc` processes over the bus, but nothing on screen says so, and the board's AGENTS cell reads 0 during a running job because (a) in-process node sessions are never counted, (b) the engine's own BackgroundBus is invisible to the count provider, and (c) the board only repaints at superstep boundaries, after the node has already finished.
design.root_cause: Three defects compound, all inside this process. (1) Non-worker agent nodes are in-process: GraphEngine.executeNode calls createSessionForNode (engine.ts:920) which uses this.sessionFactory (default core/sdk.ts createAgentSession, engine.ts:10/567) and stores the session under .kpi/runs/<job>/agents/<threadKey>/ (engine.ts:836-846); no registry records these sessions, so no surface can count them. (2) workerRole nodes spawn through a fresh `new BackgroundBus(...)` inside executeWorkerAgentNode (engine.ts:1023-1028) that is never added to the `buses` map in communicate.ts (activeBus, communicate.ts:319-330); the live count provider only sums that map (communicate.ts:287-293 → live-snapshot.ts:11-13); buildBoardModel reads liveWorkerCount() at control-plane.ts:217 and board.ts:335 prints `AGENTS ${model.agents}` — so a graph-spawned reviewer process is also counted as 0. (3) The widget is reinstalled only through LoopDependencies.onStateChange (gated-loop.ts:45), which the loop awaits after writeState at superstep boundaries (gated-loop.ts:1910, 1951, 2018; control-plane.ts:483-485); GraphEngineOptions (engine.ts:70-107) has no per-node hook, so even a correct count would be painted only when nothing is running. Worker liveness is already owned by the bus: countLiveProcesses (spawn.ts:383-391) uses the bus's injected isProcessAlive (spawn.ts:217, 233) and never reaps; the caps are per process by design (spawn.ts:37-39, 139). The fix is an in-memory, process-local registry that the engine and the parent tools feed explicitly, a pure snapshot the board and a `/agents` command render, and one engine hook so the loop repaints when a node session or worker starts or ends.

design.issue: K-π has no onboarding: a first launch shows only the harness "No models available" warning (README.md:94-104 documents a manual /login → /accounts login → /setup-kstack sequence) and there is no /onboarding command. design.root_cause: Nothing in the built-in extension factory (packages/coding-agent/src/kpi/extensions/index.ts:58-104) registers an onboarding command or a first-run session_start hook; every setup path is a separate command with its own entry (accounts/index.ts:990-1028 for /accounts login, kstack/models.ts:305-345 for /setup-kstack) and the pieces are module-private (loginAccount at accounts/index.ts:245, loginWithOfficialProvider at :198, openAuthUrl at :178; the /setup-kstack handler body is inline at kstack/models.ts:308-343; promptResearchSetup at research/setup.ts:68-84 couples the key prompts to a project-file mode write), so no caller can compose them. Research is hard-wired to two services: RESEARCH_SERVICES at research/session.ts:10, ResearchKeys :39-42, env fallbacks :60-63 and :87, mode fallback :228, endpoints.ts:13-14/32-41/103-107/136, gate.ts:134-135/145-160, setup.ts:41-51, accounts/index.ts:306-308/321, append-log.ts:79, event.schema.json:115-128, board.ts:732-738 and settings.ts:32 — adding Firecrawl requires each of those to be generalized over the service list rather than a third copy of the exa/perplexity ternaries. The revised design drops two pieces of the original that the source refutes: a "default model" step (the extension setModel at agent-session.ts:2635-2639 never persists and rejects any provider outside the harness auth snapshot, which K-π api_key pool logins never enter) and a K-π-owned writer for ~/.kpi/agent/settings.json (the harness serialises writes under a lockfile and refuses to overwrite an unparseable file; a second unlocked writer that maps parse failure to {} would be a silent, destructive catch).
